title: Concertino
identity: Cecil Leeson, Concertino for E-flat alto saxophone and wind symphonette (or chamber orchestra), with piano reduction. Aaron Eric Butler’s 1981 Ball State thesis catalog describes multiple archival states: an early reduction volume containing movements I and II, a separate volume for movement III, a later complete reduction, an E-flat alto part, and an engraver-corrected publisher copy of the full three-movement piano reduction. The two-movement description applies to one early volume, not the whole work. The PDF is a catalog of archival materials, not the musical notation itself.

evidence.claim: Opened Ball State University thesis catalog of the Cecil Leeson Archival Saxophone Collection. Printed pp. 24–29 (PDF pp. 29–34) describe several manuscript states: an early 64-page piano reduction volume with movements I–II; a companion volume for movement III; a later complete reduction; a separate E-flat alto saxophone part for all three movements; and an engraver-corrected publisher copy of the full work. The first two movement timings are listed as about 7 and 5 minutes. These are archival descriptions, not notation.
evidence.source_name: Aaron Eric Butler, Music Manuscripts and Photographs in Cecil Leeson Archival Saxophone Collection, Ball State University, printed pp. 24–29 (PDF pp. 29–34)

evidence.claim: Search result for the Ball State archive records originally listed the work for saxophone and wind symphonette, with piano reduction; this was followed to the full PDF thesis.

review_focus: Inference from the three-movement titles and work scoring: review character contrasts across Dialogue, Song and Recitation, and In a Fairly Fast Four, along with piano-reduction/orchestral balance. No note-level demands can be assessed without the score.
collection_flag: Original saxophone concerto-like work for E-flat alto saxophone and wind symphonette/chamber orchestra; a piano reduction exists. The archival catalog documents multiple manuscript versions, including a publisher-prepared full three-movement reduction.

score_links.description: Public 1981 thesis catalog inspected; it describes multiple manuscript versions, including a full three-movement publisher copy, but contains no readable Concertino notation.

gaps: The archival descriptions identify manuscripts and a publisher-prepared full three-movement version, but the PDF does not include readable Concertino notation; no public scan of the score or saxophone part was located.
The catalog reports multiple manuscript states and differing page counts; exact relation to Southern SS817 should be confirmed against the published edition.
